collection_summary: Adapted from seed #15 in datasets/pkdb_bench/docs/example_questions.txt ('For each planet in the solar system, list its named moons with their diameter in km, orbital period in days, and year of discovery.'). The staged table_title narrows the seed to the source-defined subset of named moons with documented diameter, orbital period, and discovery year — the cycle-1 audit flagged a scope/title mismatch because the seed's verbatim 'list its named moons' wording promised a complete list while the table excludes 28 named moons whose diameter or mean radius is not populated in Wikidata. Tier A (Wikidata SPARQL) extraction. Universe is the 137 IAU-named natural satellites of the eight solar-system planets that have mean radius (or diameter), orbital period, and discovery date all populated in Wikidata as of the 2026-04-28 snapshot. Diameter precedence (cycle-2 audit fix): 2 * P2120 preferred, P2386 fallback when P2120 is absent. Mercury and Venus contribute zero rows; Earth contributes one (the Moon, with 'Prehistoric' in Discovery Year because Wikidata stores no P575 for it); Mars 2 (Phobos, Deimos); Jupiter 48; Saturn 50; Uranus 23; Neptune 13. Multi-attribute (Diameter, Orbital Period, Discovery Year) over a per-planet partition exercises the calibration goal of multi_attribute_projection: the four Galilean moons, Earth's Moon, Titan, and Triton are very widely known with stable values; obscure outer-planet irregular moons (Aoede, Aitne, Erinome, Gridr, etc.) are weakly known and have measurement-precision-limited values. Result: 137 rows x 5 columns, composite PK on (Planet, Moon), 0 duplicates.
source_coverage_notes:
One Tier A source contributes rows; Wikipedia per-planet 'Moons of X' articles are cited as validation-role sources (universe-size sanity only — they do not contribute rows or values to the CSV).

Roles:
- source_urls[0] (https://query.wikidata.org/sparql): universe + value. Defines the named-moon universe via P31 = per-planet moon class and the P397/Q405 Earth-Moon UNION branch; supplies all three non-key attribute values (diameter via 2 * P2120 with P2386 fallback — see cycle-2 precedence flip in audit_response.cycle_2; orbital period via P2146 normalized to days; discovery year via P575 truncated to year, with the literal 'Prehistoric' for Q405 because Wikidata stores no P575).
- validation source — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moons_of_Mars (universe-size cross-check; Wikipedia confirms the Mars universe is exactly 2 named moons, Phobos and Deimos).
- validation source — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moons_of_Jupiter (universe-size cross-check against the named-moons section; Wikipedia lists ~57-60 named Jovian moons depending on snapshot date).
- validation source — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moons_of_Saturn (universe-size cross-check; Wikipedia lists ~64 named Saturnian moons after the 2024 IAU naming wave).
- validation source — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moons_of_Uranus (universe-size cross-check; Wikipedia confirms the canonical Shakespearean+Pope set of 27 named moons; the SPARQL pre-attribute count of 28 was reduced to 27 once the 'Uranus XXVIII' Roman-numeral provisional placeholder was filtered).
- validation source — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moons_of_Neptune (universe-size cross-check; Wikipedia confirms 14 named Neptunian moons).
- validation source — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moon (Q405 universe-size: Earth has exactly one named natural satellite).

Validation sources do not count toward source_count per the artifact-contract Source Roles convention; source_count remains 1 and source_urls remains a single-element list for the SPARQL endpoint. Wikipedia per-planet articles do mirror Wikidata in places, so the validation here is a coarse universe-size check rather than independent value verification.

Universe-size sanity check results: Mars 2 (matches Wikipedia); Jupiter pre-attribute 57 vs Wikipedia ~57-60 (within the 2024-2025 IAU-naming-wave drift band; the cycle-2 verify-rerun returned 57, two fewer than the cycle-0 staging count of 59 — Wikidata edits in the intervening period); Saturn 64 (matches); Uranus 27 (matches after Roman-numeral filter); Neptune 14 (matches). The 28-row drop between the 165-moon pre-attribute universe and the 137-row CSV reflects honest Wikidata coverage gaps in diameter / mean-radius for small inner moons (Pan, Atlas, Pandora, Prometheus on Saturn; Metis, Adrastea on Jupiter; Ophelia, Cordelia, Cressida, Bianca on Uranus; Hippocamp on Neptune; etc.) — those rows are excluded by the source_defined claim, and the staged table_title is narrowed accordingly.
decision_log:
Candidate card (Stage 1 pre-gate, then Stage 2 scored axes per instance_selection_priorities.md):
- Pre-gate verdict: PASS. Source-defined universe (IAU named moons, mechanically extractable from Wikidata's per-planet moon classes); 137 rows >> the 10-row floor; 5-column shape with 1 partition key + 1 entity key + 3 non-key attributes; strong confidence gradient (Galilean / Titan / Triton at one end vs. obscure irregular Jovian/Saturnian moons at the other); LLM-knowable for major moons; one documented temporal-edge risk in temporal_note (recent IAU naming waves and Wikidata revisions).
- Seed/provenance: ADAPTED / NARROWED from seed #15 in example_questions.txt (line 28). The cycle-0 stage used the seed verbatim, but the cycle-1 audit required narrowing the table_title to match the source-defined CSV scope (see audit_response.cycle_1). The current title says 'list its named moons that have a documented diameter, orbital period, and discovery year (the Moon is listed as Prehistoric)', which is a structural narrowing of the seed's verbatim 'list its named moons' phrasing.
- Category: multi_attribute_projection — primary because the seed shape is a per-entity multi-column SELECT with three non-key attributes whose recall confidence varies by attribute (diameter and orbital period are physically measured numerics; discovery year is a stable historical date). Secondary not set because the per-planet partition reads naturally as a key column rather than a separate query category; scaled_enumeration would imply a TOP-K shape that is not present.
- Source plan: single Tier A source (Wikidata SPARQL). Roles: universe + value. Provisional-designation filter via two regex predicates (S/-prefix and Planet-Roman-numeral). Discovery year for Q405 Moon is the literal string 'Prehistoric' because Wikidata records no P575 for it.
- Expected shape: ~137 rows x 5 columns with composite PK (Planet, Moon). Realized: 137 x 5, 0 duplicate PKs.
- Domain: Science/Astronomy — diversifies the benchmark (the snapshot in instance_selection_priorities.md flags Science/Astronomy as an absent subdomain even though the broader Science family has one registered instance).
- Risks/adaptation: (a) Recent IAU naming waves (2018-2019 Jupiter, 2024-2025 Saturn) place some named-moon items near or past LLM pretraining cutoffs; this is documented in temporal_note. (b) Wikidata's diameter coverage is partial for small inner moons (e.g., Pan, Atlas, Pandora, Prometheus on Saturn lack P2386/P2120) — these are honestly excluded by the source_defined claim. (c) Some larger irregular moons (Ananke, Cordelia, Ophelia) also lack diameter on Wikidata and are excluded; this is a Wikidata-coverage limitation, not a structural problem. (d) Mimas was a documented triaxial-body convention risk in cycles 0-1 (P2386 = 415.6 km long axis vs canonical mean diameter ~396 km from 198.2 km radius). Cycle-2 audit flipped diameter precedence to 2 * P2120 > P2386, so Mimas now reports 396.4 km. The triaxial-body convention is now consistent for every moon with a P2120 statement.
- Decision: STAGE.

Further decisions:
1) Universe filter chose `wdt:P31 ?moonClass` rather than `p:P31/ps:P31 ?moonClass` because the per-planet moon classes (Q177268, Q61702557, Q1972, Q2152, Q2139) are narrow curated classes with consistent rank usage; the deprecated-rank exception in references/sparql-gotchas.md does not apply meaningfully here. The universe-size sanity check against Wikipedia per-planet 'Moons of X' articles confirms no silent drops.
2) Earth's Moon is added via a separate UNION branch keyed on Q405 because Q405 is typed `regular moon` rather than via a dedicated `moon of Earth` class. The Q2 + Q405 BIND pair adds exactly one row to the universe.
3) 'Prehistoric' chosen as the Discovery Year sentinel for the Moon (over 0 / null / dropping the row) because (a) it preserves Earth's per-planet partition representation, (b) it is the convention used by Wikipedia's 'List of natural satellites' article, and (c) it tests an interesting calibration case where the LLM should correctly identify the absence of a recorded discovery year. Column type 'text' (cycle-1 fix; was 'date' in cycle 0) permits the 'Prehistoric' sentinel.
4) Diameter precedence is `2 * P2120 > P2386` (cycle-2 audit fix; was `P2386 > 2 * P2120` in cycles 0-1). The flipped order is the primary path because P2386 on Wikidata is editorially inconsistent for triaxial bodies (some entries store long axis, others mean diameter) and shipped at least one obvious data error (Juliet's P2386 = 936 km against a true mean diameter of ~94 km). Mean-radius doubling matches Wikipedia infobox convention for triaxial bodies. P2386 is now the fallback for moons where P2120 is absent. Of 137 rows, 62 use the radius path and 75 use the P2386 fallback. See audit_response.cycle_2.
5) Orbital periods stored as |value| in days; retrograde sign is dropped because the seed asks for 'orbital period in days' (a magnitude). Retrograde direction is recoverable from the moon's Wikidata item by readers who care.
6) Composite PK (Planet, Moon) was chosen because Moon names alone are unique across the solar system, but the per-planet partition is a load-bearing dimension of the seed question and should be a key column.

**Cycle 1 audit response (2026-04-28).** Two BLOCKING and two hygiene findings addressed; details in `audit_response.cycle_1`. BLOCKING: (a) table_title narrowed to the source-defined subset to match the actual CSV scope; (b) Discovery Year column type changed from 'date' to 'text' to accommodate the 'Prehistoric' sentinel. HYGIENE: (c) db_analog now spells out the IS NOT NULL filter; (d) Wikipedia per-planet 'Moons of X' articles are now declared as validation-role sources in the Roles: block per the artifact-contract convention. CSV row data unchanged.
normalization_decisions: Planet names use English Wikidata labels (Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune). Moon names use English Wikidata labels (Wikipedia and IAU canonical names: Io, Europa, Ganymede, Callisto, Titan, Enceladus, Triton, Miranda, Phobos, Deimos, Moon, etc.). Diameter values are in kilometers, preserved at Wikidata-stored precision (no extra rounding). Diameter precedence (cycle-2 audit fix): the post-processor prefers 2 * P2120 (mean radius doubled) over P2386 and uses P2386 only as fallback when P2120 is absent. Cycles 0-1 used the inverse precedence; cycle-2 flipped it to fix Juliet's 936-km Wikidata data error and to align with Wikipedia's mean-diameter convention for triaxial bodies (Mimas 396.4 km from radius doubling rather than 415.6 km long axis). Orbital periods are in absolute days (negative retrograde values are taken as |value|), preserved at Wikidata-stored precision. Discovery year is a 4-digit year string for non-Earth moons (e.g., '1610' for the Galilean moons, '1877' for Phobos and Deimos, '1789' for Mimas / Enceladus, etc.) and the literal string 'Prehistoric' for the Moon. Sort order is (Planet ASC, Moon ASC). The Discovery Year column is typed 'text' (cycle-1 audit fix; was 'date' in cycle 0) because the column carries a non-numeric sentinel ('Prehistoric') for the Moon and the benchmark's 'date' type is reserved for true date / year values. The 'text' typing is registration-safe and matches the actual cell shape.
open_questions: 1) Wikidata's diameter / mean-radius coverage is incomplete for small inner moons of Saturn (Pan, Atlas, Pandora, Prometheus) and a handful of Jupiter / Uranus / Neptune irregulars; those rows are honestly excluded by the source_defined claim, but a future audit pass could supplement from per-moon Wikipedia articles to convert this to a partially_supplemented instance. The 137-row scope is preserved across cycles 0-2. 2) Mimas was reported at 415.6 km (P2386 long axis) in cycles 0-1; cycle-2 flipped diameter precedence to 2*P2120 and Mimas is now 396.4 km (canonical mean diameter). 3) Three Jupiter moons (Eirene, Pandia, Ersa) and several Saturn moons received IAU names in 2018-2019 and 2024-2025; their P575 dates may be near LLM pretraining cutoffs. The temporal_note flags this as a documented risk rather than a blocker. 4) The narrowed table_title says 'For each planet in the solar system, list its named moons that have a documented diameter, orbital period, and discovery year'; Mercury and Venus contribute zero rows because they have no natural satellites at all. The empty per-planet partitions are faithful to the universe rather than a data gap. 5) Recent IAU practice has named some retrograde Jovian moons in batches (e.g., Eirene, Eupheme); their orbital periods are stored as negative on Wikidata. The pipeline takes |value|, which matches the title's 'orbital period in days' phrasing. 6) Cupid (Uranus) reports 36 km in the CSV (Wikidata P2120 = 18 km doubled = 36 km), but Wikipedia's Cupid article gives ~17.8 km mean diameter assuming albedo ~0.07. The 36 km value is also published in the same Cupid literature under a darker-albedo assumption (~0.04). The CSV value is the higher Wikidata-stored estimate; this is honest source_defined-from-Wikidata, but a future curator could note the albedo-assumption uncertainty in temporal_note or supplement from Wikipedia to take the lower estimate (which would convert this to partially_supplemented). 7) The Wikidata snapshot moves; if a future curator re-runs the SPARQL the row count may shift by a small number as new moons are named or new diameter / radius values are added. Document the new snapshot date and any per-planet count delta in decision_log on each rebuild.

blocking_addressed: Scope/title mismatch — the cycle-0 title 'list its named moons' over-promised relative to the staged CSV, which excludes 28 named moons whose diameter or mean radius is missing on Wikidata. Cycle-1 fix: narrowed table_title to 'list its named moons that have a documented diameter, orbital period, and discovery year, with their diameter in km, orbital period in days, and year of discovery.' This matches the source_defined claim and the actual row set without changing the CSV. The narrowing path was preferred over the supplement path because the dropped moons would require per-moon Wikipedia entity pages and would convert the instance to partially_supplemented; the source-defined narrowing keeps a single Tier A source with honest scope.

Discovery Year typed as 'date' but contains the literal sentinel 'Prehistoric' for the Moon — cycle-1 fix: changed column_types['Discovery Year'] from 'date' to 'text'. The 'text' typing is registration-safe, matches the actual cell shape (mostly 4-digit year strings + one 'Prehistoric'), and avoids forcing a numeric/date interpretation that would be false for one row.
hygiene_addressed: db_analog now reflects the complete-value filter explicitly: added 'AND diameter_km IS NOT NULL AND orbital_period_days IS NOT NULL AND discovery_year IS NOT NULL' clauses. With Discovery Year typed as 'text' and 'Prehistoric' as a non-null sentinel for the Moon, the IS NOT NULL filter accurately captures the source-defined scope.

Wikipedia per-planet 'Moons of X' articles, previously cited only as prose universe-size sanity checks in source_coverage_notes, are now declared as validation-role sources in the Roles: block per the artifact-contract Source Roles convention. They do not count toward source_count (validation sources never do) but are now first-class, named provenance for the universe-count claims.

decision_log cleanup follow-up: removed stale cycle-0 wording ('VERBATIM seed #15... title is unchanged from the seed' and 'Column type date permits the string form'), replaced with cycle-1-current language ('ADAPTED / NARROWED from seed #15' and 'Column type text (cycle-1 fix; was date in cycle 0)'). No CSV row changes.

table_title tightened to acknowledge the Moon's Prehistoric exception inline: '...discovery year (the Moon is listed as Prehistoric)...'. The temporal_note already documented the Moon-as-Prehistoric special case; the in-title parenthetical is the auditor-preferred light tightening rather than a wholesale rewrite.

blocking_addressed: Juliet (Uranus) diameter was 936 km in the cycle-0/cycle-1 CSV (a Wikidata P2386 data error — Wikipedia's Juliet (moon) article gives mean diameter ~94 km from dimensions 150 x 74 x 74 km). The error propagated because the post-processor preferred P2386 over 2 * P2120. Cycle-2 fix (curation-side): flipped the diameter precedence rule in the SPARQL post-processor to prefer 2 * P2120 (mean radius doubled) over P2386, with P2386 retained as fallback when P2120 is absent. Re-ran the SPARQL pipeline and regenerated the CSV. Verified Juliet 936 -> 106 km (= 2 * P2120 = 2 * 53 km, in the right magnitude range against Wikipedia's ~94 km). Mimas verified 415.6 -> 396.4 km (now canonical mean diameter from 198.2 km radius rather than long axis). Cupid verified 36 -> 36 km (unchanged: Wikidata P2120 = 18 km doubled = 36; Wikidata stores the higher albedo-uncertainty estimate, which is also published in literature and is honestly source_defined-from-Wikidata). The SPARQL file's narrative comment was updated to declare the new precedence rule explicitly, citing the Juliet typo and the triaxial-body convention as motivations.
hygiene_addressed: Cupid (Uranus) diameter is 36 km in Wikidata vs Wikipedia's ~17.8 km mean diameter (assuming albedo ~0.07). Both values appear in the same Cupid literature under different albedo assumptions; Wikidata stores the larger value. Cycle-2 fix: documented the albedo-assumption uncertainty as open_question item 6 so future curators can choose to switch to the lower estimate (which would convert this instance to partially_supplemented). No CSV change for cycle 2.

draft.json::_extraction_notes, curation.json::normalization_decisions, curation.json::open_questions, and curation.json::source_coverage_notes Roles: block were all updated to declare the cycle-2 precedence flip and to remove stale cycle-0/cycle-1 'P2386 with P2120 fallback' phrasing (now '2 * P2120 with P2386 fallback'). Per-planet split of which path was used (radius / fallback) was added to _extraction_notes: Earth 1/0, Mars 1/1, Jupiter 16/32, Saturn 15/35, Uranus 21/2, Neptune 8/5.

Cycle-2 re-audit follow-up: replaced stale cycle-0/cycle-1 Mimas-as-long-axis wording in decision_log item (d) with cycle-2-current language noting the convention is now consistent for every moon with a P2120 statement.

Cycle-2 re-audit follow-up: corrected source_coverage_notes universe-size sanity result for Jupiter from 'pre-attribute 59 vs Wikipedia ~57-60' to 'pre-attribute 57 vs Wikipedia ~57-60', noting that the cycle-2 verify-rerun returned 57 (two fewer than the cycle-0 staging count of 59 due to Wikidata edits in the intervening period).
suggestion_addressed: Mimas 415.6 km long-axis vs ~396.4 km mean-diameter convention drift (cycle-1 audit SUGGESTION) is resolved by the cycle-2 precedence flip; Mimas now reports 396.4 km from radius doubling. The convention is now consistent across all triaxial bodies that have a P2120 statement on Wikidata.
P2386 vs 2 * P2120 precedence (cycle-1 audit SUGGESTION + structural lever) is addressed by the cycle-2 fix above. P2386 is now the fallback rather than the primary path.

Cycle-2 re-audit SUGGESTION: clarify that table_title's 'documented' means 'present in the cited Wikidata source set'. Adopted: added a one-sentence scope clarification to draft.json::_extraction_notes rather than further amending the title (which already carries one parenthetical for the Moon's Prehistoric exception; a second parenthetical would be cluttered). Decision recorded here so a future reviewer does not re-litigate.
cycle_2.row_count_delta: 0 rows added or removed; 137 -> 137. The precedence flip changed values in 62 rows where 2 * P2120 was preferred over P2386 (Earth Moon; Mars Deimos; 16 Jupiter rows; 15 Saturn rows; 21 Uranus rows incl. Juliet/Mimas/Cupid; 8 Neptune rows). The remaining 75 rows had no P2120 in Wikidata and used P2386 fallback, so their values are unchanged from cycles 0-1.
